newsitem.title: FINLAND: Goldman finds forestry stocks bounce fragile.
newsitem.headline: Goldman finds forestry stocks bounce fragile.

text.p: A recent jump in pulp and paper stocks is understandable but the industry environment does not indicate a sustained upturn in the pulp and paper cycle, brokerage Goldman Sachs said in a note to investors.

"We stick to our cautious stance and recommend investors to market weight the sector at this point; if share prices gain another five-10 percent before the end of the year we would view this as an excellent exit opportunity," it said in the note dated December 2 and received on Tuesday.
Goldman saw three main reasons behind recent forestry gains: expectations of a breakthrough in the cycle, investors seeking recently static or weak stocks and the strength of the dollar.
"A trading-related bounce was not illogical in the sentiment-driven sector," it said, citing a fall of some 15 percent in September against strength in most markets.

Goldman said it was quite possible to see momentum in fine paper -- with manufacturers likely to seek higher prices of up to 10 percent in January -- helping to swing sentiment near-term. But it was sceptical about a sustainable upswing.

"Paper demand is still jittery," it said, adding that fine paper faces much new capacity. Norscan pulp stocks were high around 1.8 million tonnes at end-October and could climb further in the first quarter of 1997, Goldman said.
"We do not see a strong and broad-based turn before the second half of 1997 at the earliest," Goldman said, adding that its forecasts point to lower forestry company earnings next year.
